sections.text: The United States held its first deep-sea mining lease auction off American Samoa, selling two seabed tracts to sole bidder Wetstone US Ventures for $3m each. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: At the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey, the African Group of Negotiators pushed to triple adaptation finance by 2035. The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations. European Union officials stated that the focus should be on deploying already pledged climate funds rather than establishing new targets. Meanwhile, 23 African countries have not submitted National Adaptation Plans to the UN.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Sub-Saharan Africa requires around $51bn annually for adaptation, but developing nations received only about 10% of needed global funds in 2024. Without National Adaptation Plans, securing climate financing is more difficult for vulnerable nations suffering from severe droughts and floods. However, experts note that lack of support and technical capacity prevents these countries from preparing the required plans.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: African negotiators continue to push for increased funding commitments. The European Union called for improvements in helping developing countries access existing climate funds that remain undeployed.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Outgoing Republican senator John Cornyn blocked Donald Trump's nomination of T Elliot Gaiser for a district court in northern Texas. This followed a heated verbal argument on the Senate floor between Cornyn and fellow Texas Republican senator Ted Cruz regarding the nomination. Cornyn withheld his blue slip, preventing the Senate judiciary committee from moving Gaiser forward.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The block disrupts Republican plans to approve Trump's judicial nominations before Congress recesses and Democrats take control of Congress in January. Cruz stated that leaving the seat vacant would give it to the Democrats. The justice department criticized Cornyn for choosing political obstruction, while the Heritage Foundation president also condemned the decision.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The International Court of Justice ruled that genocide was committed against the Rohingya people in Myanmar. The court inferred genocidal intent from the actions of Myanmar's security forces and local militias.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The judgement clarifies the evidentiary standard required to prove genocide. This decision has implications for other cases, including South Africa's case against Israel regarding Gaza. The UK called for UN Security Council action and expelled Myanmar's defence attache in London.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The ICJ ordered Myanmar to make reparations to the Rohingya people. However, the court lacks enforcement mechanisms, and the Myanmar government is unlikely to accept the ruling quietly. Any UN Security Council resolution could face a veto from China or Russia.
